facts.claim: Red A/D versus White B/C across all grades; first-year class ranking bonuses/penalties +50,0,-50,-100, losing team -100 class points; recommended relay triple points.
Advocates opponent scouting, concealed lineups, stamina preparation and risk planning; distinguishes preparation from rule exploitation.
Class A and D coordinate minimally; Ryuen refuses overt Class B coordination, which Ayanokoji regards as a possible strategic feint.
Sudou beats Shibata in obstacle race despite Shibata closing distance; narrative considers them closely matched, Shibata possibly faster on pure running.

Ryuen and Kinoshita present an accusation of deliberate collision and demand one million private points; Horikita disputes intent and suspects a staged trap. Do not classify the contested allegation as established fact.
Horikita seeks out Sudou after he leaves the festival, recognizing both his value and her own leadership failures.
Ayanokoji enters relay as paid substitute after Miyake reports ankle injury; dialogue reveals his participation was privately planned with Hirata.
Sudou builds at least fifteen-meter opening relay lead; Hirata maintains it; subsequent runners lose positions, with Class D seventh before Kushida passes to anchor.
Ayanokoji and Manabu race at full speed after Manabu waits for his baton; a fallen runner obstructs Ayanokoji and Manabu pulls ahead. No clean uncontaminated speed ranking is justified.
Red Team wins; first-year class rank B>C>A>D. Net class-point change B 0, C -100, A -50, D -100. Shibata Sou wins first-year MVP; Sudou not MVP despite winning individual events.
Sudou promises to avoid unjustified violence, with justification assessed by Horikita or a third party; Horikita permits first-name address despite his MVP loss.
